_evidence.join: Directed first-response audit over every one-to-one conversation (12 lanes; chat search never returns them). Seventy-five second-read requests carry the firm's standing phrasing. A request is timely when the person asked first comes back to the asker — later in that same lane or by directed email — by the end of the next working day. Exactly three miss that deadline: 1780692153 (2026-06-05 Fri, Sofia Ramirez -> Grace Adeyemi), 1781024940 (2026-06-09 Tue, Grace Adeyemi -> Peter Novak), and 1782262238 (2026-06-23 Tue, Marcus Liang -> Sofia Ramirez). All three eventually receive late Slack replies, which the retained ledger cites without reclassifying them as timely.
_evidence.decoys: Sixty-seven requests drew their first qualifying answer the same day, including request 1871852's same-day directed Gmail response. Five first came back after the request day but by the next-working-day deadline. One Friday request first gets a Saturday Slack response; it is timely because Saturday precedes Monday's deadline. A Slack-only or calendar-day reading misclassifies these cross-surface and weekend records.
_evidence.grading: The primary 75-row response ledger carries 0.72 with normalized multiset F1 plus exact certification. The exception summaries, aggregates, and ledger reconciliation are separately graded; a headline-only answer cannot reach half credit.
